using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Dictionary;

public sealed partial class WordNetExampleUsageHintService : IUsageHintService
{
    public UsageHintResult GetHint(DictionaryLookupResult lookup, SenseRankingResult ranking, string targetWord)
    {
        // An abstaining ranker may still expose a study-only comparison, but
        // every example must remain attached to its own sense. This keeps the
        // main definition undecided while giving the learner a useful way to
        // distinguish the candidates.
        var isMultiSenseComparison = ranking.SelectedSense is null;
        var senses = isMultiSenseComparison
            ? lookup.Senses ?? []
            : new[] { ranking.SelectedSense! };

        // A partial comparison is not neutral: displaying evidence for only
        // one candidate can quietly recreate the sense choice that the main
        // card deliberately abstained from. Restrict this study-only form to
        // a complete, compact two-way contrast.
        if (isMultiSenseComparison && senses.Count != 2)
        {
            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }

        var hints = senses
            .Select(sense =>
            {
                var examples = (sense.EnglishExamples ?? [])
                    .Where(candidate => ContainsTarget(candidate, targetWord))
                    .Select(candidate => ToShortHint(candidate, targetWord))
                    .Where(hint => hint.Length > 0)
                    .Distinct(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
                    .Take(2)
                    .ToArray();
                if (examples.Length == 0)
                {
                    return (Text: string.Empty, Examples: Array.Empty<string>());
                }

                var text = isMultiSenseComparison
                    ? $"{sense.PartOfSpeech}. {sense.ShortDefinition}：{string.Join(" · ", examples)}"
                    : string.Join(" · ", examples);
                return (Text: text, Examples: examples);
            })
            .Where(hint => hint.Text.Length > 0)
            .GroupBy(hint => hint.Text, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            .Select(group => group.First())
            .Take(2)
            .ToArray();
        if (isMultiSenseComparison && hints.Length != senses.Count)
        {
            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }
        if (hints.Length == 0)
        {
            // A single-sense entry may have no examples but still carry a
            // useful, source-backed English concept definition. Keep this
            // fallback bounded and study-only; never use it to choose among
            // competing senses.
            if (!isMultiSenseComparison && senses.Count == 1)
            {
                var definition = (senses[0].EnglishDefinitions ?? [])
                    .Select(CleanDefinition)
                    .FirstOrDefault(candidate => candidate.Length is >= 20 and <= 160);
                if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(definition))
                {
                    return new UsageHintResult(
                        $"核心概念  {definition}",
                        "Open English WordNet 2025；定�?,
                        0.80);
                }
            }

            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }

        var examples = hints.SelectMany(hint => hint.Examples).ToArray();
        var exactCoverage = examples.Count(example => HasExactTarget(example, targetWord)) / (double)examples.Length;
        var confidence = 0.75 + exactCoverage * 0.15;
        var verification = exactCoverage == 1
            ? "例句直含目标�?
            : "例句含常规词�?;
        return new UsageHintResult(
            string.Join(" · ", hints.Select(hint => hint.Text)),
            $"Open English WordNet 2025；{verification}",
            confidence);
    }

    private static string ToShortHint(string example, string targetWord)
    {
        var words = WordToken().Matches(example).Select(match => match.Value).ToArray();
        if (words.Length == 0)
        {
            return string.Empty;
        }

        var targetIndex = Array.FindIndex(words, word => IsTargetForm(word, targetWord));
        var start = targetIndex < 0 ? 0 : Math.Max(0, targetIndex - 3);
        var end = targetIndex < 0 ? Math.Min(words.Length, 7) : Math.Min(words.Length, targetIndex + 4);
        var prefix = start > 0 ? "�? : string.Empty;
        var suffix = end < words.Length ? "�? : string.Empty;
        return $"{prefix}{string.Join(" ", words[start..end]).ToLowerInvariant()}{suffix}";
    }

    private static bool ContainsTarget(string text, string targetWord) =>
        WordToken().Matches(text).Any(match => IsTargetForm(match.Value, targetWord));

    private static bool HasExactTarget(string text, string targetWord) =>
        WordToken().Matches(text).Any(match => match.Value.Equals(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

    private static string CleanDefinition(string value) =>
        Regex.Replace(value.Trim(), "\\s+", " ").Trim(' ', '.', ';', ':');

    private static bool IsTargetForm(string word, string targetWord)
    {
        if (word.Equals(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
        {
            return true;
        }

        // Do not let a prefix match turn "go" into evidence for "good".
        // This is intentionally a small inflection whitelist rather than a
        // general stemmer: a displayed example must visibly contain the word
        // or a conventional surface inflection of it.
        if (word.StartsWith(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && IsInflectionSuffix(word[targetWord.Length..]))
        {
            return true;
        }

        return targetWord.EndsWith('e')
            && word.StartsWith(targetWord[..^1], StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && IsInflectionSuffix(word[(targetWord.Length - 1)..]);
    }

    private static bool IsInflectionSuffix(string suffix) => suffix.Equals("s", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("es", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("d", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("ed", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("ing", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("er", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("est", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    [GeneratedRegex("[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)?")]
    private static partial Regex WordToken();
}

using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Presentation;

public static class LookupCardTextFormatter
{
    public static string Frequency(int band) => band switch
    {
        3 => "★★�?,
        2 => "★★�?,
        1 => "★☆�?,
        _ => string.Empty,
    };

    public static string Breakdown(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.WordBreakdown) ? string.Empty : $"词基/构词  {presentation.WordBreakdown}";

    public static string Family(LookupPresentation presentation) => presentation.WordFamily is { Count: > 0 }
        ? $"词族/词形  {string.Join(" · ", presentation.WordFamily.Take(3))}"
        : string.Empty;

    public static string Usage(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.ContextHint) ? string.Empty : $"用法/语境  {presentation.ContextHint}";

    public static string Evidence(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.InsightEvidence)
            ? string.Empty
            : $"证据  {presentation.InsightEvidence}";

    public static string ContextAlignment(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        presentation.IsContextAligned ? "整句句意对齐：已用于筛�? : "整句句意对齐：未用于筛�?;

    public static IReadOnlyList<string> VisibleLines(LookupPresentation presentation)
    {
        var core = new[]
        {
            $"{presentation.Title} {Frequency(presentation.FrequencyBand)}".Trim(),
            presentation.PrimaryDefinition,
            presentation.IsError ? string.Empty : ContextAlignment(presentation),
        }.Where(line => line.Length > 0).ToList();

        // Keep the first screen compact: sentence meaning and usage outrank
        // study metadata. Show at most one optional metadata block so the
        // card never grows beyond five visible information blocks.
        var metadata = Breakdown(presentation);
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(metadata))
        {
            metadata = Family(presentation);
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(metadata))
        {
            core.Add(metadata);
        }

        var evidence = Evidence(presentation);
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(evidence))
        {
            core.Add(evidence);
        }

        // Provenance is part of the trust contract for learning content. When
        // the five-block first screen is full, keep the source-bearing line
        // and let the optional usage example yield space for it.
        var usage = Usage(presentation);
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(usage) && core.Count < 5)
        {
            core.Add(usage);
        }

        return core.Take(5).ToArray();
    }
}

 succeeded in 1260ms:
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\RealtimeTranslateCodex\dictionary.tsv`

Dictionary rows use:

```text
word	definition1; definition2
```

Load order is: small embedded fallback dictionary, bundled ECDICT dictionary, then the user override dictionary. Later entries override earlier entries with the same word.

Vocabulary cards use a structured local lexicon generated from ECDICT and Open English WordNet evidence. The runtime keeps Chinese short senses, parts of speech, English definitions/examples, and BNC/FRQ frequency bands. A second build step fuses precision-filtered MorphyNet relations with selected MorphoLex analyses. Only reviewed modern derivations, useful compounds, and inflectional forms are displayed; uncertain analyses are omitted and replaced by a short WordNet usage/context hint.

Word lookup captures two in-memory crops from one screenshot: a tight word crop and a wider line-context crop. The line context ranks senses locally. A sense is promoted only when its evidence clearly wins; otherwise the card displays compact numbered senses instead of guessing.

The deterministic 200-word advanced-vocabulary audit is stored in `tests/Data/rendered-card-audit.tsv`. Tests enforce 100% translations, visible frequency bands, at least 90% family/form coverage, at least 35% reviewed morphology coverage, and at least 95% visible morphology-or-usage coverage. Regression cases also reject known false relationships.

To regenerate the bundled dictionary from ECDICT:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\tools\Import-Ecdict.ps1
```

## 目标

- 上下�?normalized WER �?%，或关键内容词准确率 �?2%�?

- 依赖上下文的词义 Top-1 �?0%；低质量上下文强行影响主释义�?0�?
- P95 从松开选择到基础�?�? 秒�?

必须探索并按实证选择：行�?OCR 输出（含几何位置）、多尺度与多预处理结果、候选行融合、以选区为锚点的字幕区裁剪、以及可信度门控。不得把首个非空 OCR 结果当作成功；不得通过词典猜测伪�?OCR 原文；低可信上下文必须明确降级�?

## 学习型卡片的完成定义

卡片分为两层�?

- **首屏（继续读剧情�?*：原�?词形、当前句义、词性、短语或句子功能、上下文可信状态。最多五块；网络不可用也必须出现�?

## 学习质量量化门槛

对至�?30 个真实游戏词建立学习评测集（含普通词、抽象词、词形变化、搭配、专有称谓和多义词）。每项有可验证的核心释义、至少一个不可接受的空泛/错误解释及来源�?

Context ranking and abstention remain outside this change.
- Independent review: fresh read-only reviewer decision was `insufficient-evidence`. It verified that only definition hooks were removed and the 90 example hooks remained, but found the 200-row audit structural rather than a learning-quality measure. Report: reviewer response for committed `6ed9cd0` in this run; no acceptance report is eligible.
- Regressions/limits: lower hook coverage is intentional and does not establish learner usefulness. Before/after learning outputs are preserved at `artifacts/learning-example-gate-before-20260901.tsv` and `artifacts/learning-example-gate-after-20260901.tsv`.

index e59e3ff..d3d12c0 100644
--- a/docs/agentic-loop-status.md
+++ b/docs/agentic-loop-status.md
@@ -1,15 +1,15 @@
 # Agentic Loop Status
 
-Updated: 2026-09-01 03:42:00
+Updated: 2026-09-01 04:08:00
 
-- Run: agent iteration 18
+- Run: agent iteration 20
 - Stage: improving usable context OCR and learning-card quality
 - Goal: reliable sentence understanding plus memorable word learning
 - Independent review: required after each relevant committed change
 - Completion: automatic threshold or user acceptance
-- Hypothesis: single-sense WordNet entries without examples can still provide a useful learning layer when one bounded English definition is shown as a sourced core concept; this should increase memorable, evidence-backed clues without steering sense selection.
-- Change: `WordNetExampleUsageHintService` now emits `核心概念` only for a single sense and a 20-160 character WordNet definition. Multi-sense comparisons and short/weak definitions still omit the insight. Added a regression test for the definition-only fallback.
-- Metric delta: rendered 200-word audit sourced learning hooks increased from 90/200 (45.0%) in `artifacts/card-audit-hypothesis.tsv` to 161/200 (80.5%) in `artifacts/card-audit-hypothesis-after.tsv`; this clears the 70% coverage target. Existing OCR replay evidence is unchanged at 20/20 exact and 14/16 labelled context Top-1. Tests: 22/22 passed; solution build 0 warnings, 0 errors.
-- Real examples: `go` with WordNet definition `move from one place to another` now shows a source-labelled core concept while keeping the Chinese gloss `移动`; `bark` with no trusted context remains an abstention and does not receive a guessed main sense; a one-word definition such as `move` is still omitted as too weak.
-- Regressions: no first-screen definition, context alignment, or multi-sense abstention changes observed; 39/200 audit words still omit learning hooks by design because no bounded sourced example/definition is available.
-- Next question: have an independent blind reviewer judge whether the new English core concepts help learners beyond the Chinese gloss, and measure the learning-layer pass rate and any cases where the definition merely repeats the gloss.
+- Hypothesis: a bounded WordNet definition is not, by itself, a dependable learning insight because it can merely restate the Chinese gloss; requiring a source-backed example containing the target word or a verified regular inflection will remove weak claims while retaining useful word-level evidence.
+- Change: removed the definition-only fallback from `WordNetExampleUsageHintService`. The learning layer now abstains when no target-bearing WordNet example exists; it does not affect sense ranking or first-screen meanings. Added a regression that `go` with only `move from one place to another` produces no learning hook.
+- Metric delta: deterministic 200-word rendered-card audit changed from 161/200 source-bearing hooks before to 90/200 after. The 71 removed hooks were exactly all definition-only hooks (71 -> 0); verified-example hooks stayed 90/200 (90 -> 90). Focused suite: 23/23 passing. Release solution build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
+- Real examples: `go` with Chinese gloss `移动` and only the definition `move from one place to another` now omits the learning layer rather than presenting a gloss repeat. `dwindle` retains `their savings dwindled away`; `bark` still offers a two-sense comparison only when each sense has a target-bearing example. Context ranking and abstention remain outside this change.
+- Regressions/limits: lower hook coverage is intentional and does not establish learner usefulness. This checkout contains no real-game screenshot files, manual transcription set, 50-screenshot gold corpus, or completed independent card judgments; OCR metrics therefore remain unmeasured here. Before/after learning outputs are preserved at `artifacts/learning-example-gate-before-20260901.tsv` and `artifacts/learning-example-gate-after-20260901.tsv`.
+- Next question: can a sourced 30-word real-game learning evaluation establish whether the retained target-bearing examples are useful memory cues rather than just accurate usage snippets?

docs\sentence-explanation.md:18:The feature reuses selection, screenshot capture, OCR, tray, and hotkey infrastructure. It adds a separate text-oriented flow:
docs\sentence-explanation.md:20:`selection -> screenshot -> OCR text lines -> AI explanation service -> explanation panel`
docs\sentence-explanation.md:49:Keep the existing word lookup JSONL unchanged. Add a separate `records/explanations.jsonl` file for text explanation events. Each record should include timestamp, source text, translation, notes, selection rectangle, screenshot path, and error text when applicable.
docs\roadmap.md:16:- The feature should reuse selection, screenshot, OCR, archive, and hotkey plumbing, but use separate text post-processing, explanation, and presentation services.
docs\roadmap.md:26:Decision: implement as a separate F6 text explanation flow backed by a configurable AI API, keeping normal word lookup offline and independent.

docs\agentic-loop-status.md:8:- Independent review: completed for `6ed9cd0`; verdict `insufficient-evidence`
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:10:- Hypothesis: a bounded WordNet definition is not, by itself, a dependable learning insight because it can merely restate the Chinese gloss; requiring a source-backed example containing the target word or a verified regular inflection will remove weak claims while retaining useful word-level evidence.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:12:- Metric delta: deterministic 200-word rendered-card audit changed from 161/200 source-bearing hooks before to 90/200 after. The 71 removed hooks were exactly all definition-only hooks (71 -> 0); verified-example hooks stayed 90/200 (90 -> 90). Focused suite: 23/23 passing. Release solution build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:14:- Independent review: fresh read-only reviewer decision was `insufficient-evidence`. It verified that only definition hooks were removed and the 90 example hooks remained, but found the 200-row audit structural rather than a learning-quality measure. It also identified 22/90 retained hooks that use heuristic regular-inflection matching and therefore require factual/provenance audit. Report: reviewer response for committed `6ed9cd0` in this run; no acceptance report is eligible.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:15:- Regressions/limits: lower hook coverage is intentional and does not establish learner usefulness. This checkout contains no real-game screenshot files, manual transcription set, 50-screenshot gold corpus, or completed independent card judgments; OCR metrics therefore remain unmeasured here. Before/after learning outputs are preserved at `artifacts/learning-example-gate-before-20260901.tsv` and `artifacts/learning-example-gate-after-20260901.tsv`.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:16:- Next question: on a sourced 30-word real-game set, do independent reviewers judge the 90 retained example hooks useful beyond the gloss at >=80%, with zero factual/provenance errors?

docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:44:对每个改�?OCR、上下文选择、可信度或学习卡架构的提交，runner 启动一个全新、只�?reviewer agent。评委必须审查截图、金标准、前后输出和实际卡片，只能输�?`accept`、`reject` �?`insufficient-evidence`，不能修改文件，也不能仅凭实现者的文字或单元测试认可方案�?docs\agent-loop-status.md:5:- Run: isolated replay evidence by accepting `--replay-output` in the app and assigning each verifier invocation and child replay a unique temporary lookup-record file. `Verify-ReplayCorpus.ps1` also recognizes the current explicit-abstention prefix. This prevents concurrent replay processes from shifting one card's output onto another source index.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:6:- Evidence: the clean real Debug replay of all 20 game screenshots completed with zero timeouts/failures, `ocr_exact=20/20`, `dictionary_found=20/20`, `top1_sense=15/16`, available context `16/16`, context top-1 `15/16`, and labelled abstentions `4/4`: `artifacts/blind-review-source-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json`. `dotnet build RealtimeTranslateCodex.sln --no-restore` completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; the executable suite passed 19/19.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:7:- Blind-review evidence: `artifacts/blind-card-review-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json` was generated from that clean source. It contains 20 actual cards with all 20 decisions and rationales blank; card fields contain no expected sense/outcome or automated verdict. It is genuinely unreviewed and includes the new uncertainty wording.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:8:- Remaining blocker: an independent human must complete that packet’s blinded `understandable` / `unclear` / `should-abstain` decision and rationale. No code change can supply this judgement; without it the product has neither the required human result nor the required 16 directly understood cards.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:9:- Next: have a reviewer complete `artifacts/blind-card-review-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json` without opening `tests/Data/replay-expected.json`, then run `pwsh -File tools/Test-BlindCardReview.ps1 -ReviewPath <completed-review.json> -SummaryPath artifacts/blind-review-source-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json -OutputPath artifacts/blind-review-reconciliation-<date>.json`. artifacts\agent-review-log.md:21:You are an independent, read-only and deliberately skeptical reviewer. Review the latest committed change against docs/agentic-loop-goal.md. Inspect real screenshot evidence, manual transcription data, before/after OCR outputs, actual rendered cards, learning-insight provenance, and the change itself. Do not edit files. Reject claims based only on non-empty OCR, a longer card, generic AI prose, unit tests, or the implementer's narrative. Check whether context is genuinely readable and safe, and whether learning content helps remember the word itself rather than repeating a Chinese gloss or inventing a story. Return exactly: DECISION: accept|reject|insufficient-evidence; then concise evidence, metric validity, factual/provenance problems, regressions, and the single next question.

artifacts\agent-review-log.md:8641:artifacts\agent-review-log.md:21:You are an independent, read-only and deliberately skeptical reviewer. Review the latest committed change against docs/agentic-loop-goal.md. Inspect real screenshot evidence, manual transcription data, before/after OCR outputs, actual rendered cards, learning-insight provenance, and the change itself. Do not edit files. Reject claims based only on non-empty OCR, a longer card, generic AI prose, unit tests, or the implementer's narrative. Check whether context is genuinely readable and safe, and whether learning content helps remember the word itself rather than repeating a Chinese gloss or inventing a story. Return exactly: DECISION: accept|reject|insufficient-evidence; then concise evidence, metric validity, factual/provenance problems, regressions, and the single next question.

artifacts\agent-review-log.md:10187:docs\agentic-loop-status.md:14:- Regressions/limits: no build or existing test regressions; the 20-card blind-review files still contain no completed human decisions, so learning-layer judge pass rate and source factuality are not yet independently established. artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20819: - Hypothesis: legacy four-column word-card rows attach scenario-specific context hints to MorphoLex, although that source does not support those invented scenes; omitting unproven hints should improve learning factuality without removing morphology clues.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20820: - Change: `MorphemeWordInsightService` now keeps context hints only when a row has an explicit evidence-source column. Legacy rows still expose breakdown/family with the conservative MorphoLex label; explicit sourced rows retain their hint and confidence.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20821:-- Metric delta: focused suite 20/20 passed; solution build 0 warnings/0 errors. The 200-card audit remains 189/200 evidence-labelled, while unproven legacy usage hints fall from 0/200 in the exported visible audit (the prior export did not surface them) and are now structurally omitted rather than attributed. This is a provenance-safety metric, not proof of learning usefulness.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20822:+- Metric delta: focused suite 20/20 passed; solution build 0 warnings/0 errors. The production TSV has 11 non-empty legacy context-hint rows; they are now omitted unless explicitly sourced. The existing 200-card audit remains 189/200 evidence-labelled but predates this commit, so it cannot establish a before/after learning delta. This is a provenance-safety change, not proof of learning usefulness.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20823: - Real examples: the production legacy row for `ineffable` keeps its MorphoLex morphology/family but no longer claims the scene hint `sacred mysteries`; an explicitly sourced fixture (`WordNet examples`) still preserves its hint. Existing `bark` dog/tree and abstention contexts are unchanged.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20824: - Regressions/limits: removing legacy hints may reduce memory cues for some cards; no independent reviewer has yet judged the trade-off, and the 30-word learning set plus 50-screenshot OCR gates remain incomplete. The 75% MorphoLex default is still a row-level fallback, not an audit.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:20826:+- Independent review: `insufficient-evidence` (reviewer report: no screenshots, completed blind decisions, 30-word evaluation, or post-commit card export; explicit fixture path is not production evidence).

artifacts\agent-review-log.md:21274:You are an independent, read-only and deliberately skeptical reviewer. Review the latest committed change against docs/agentic-loop-goal.md. Inspect real screenshot evidence, manual transcription data, before/after OCR outputs, actual rendered cards, learning-insight provenance, and the change itself. Do not edit files. Reject claims based only on non-empty OCR, a longer card, generic AI prose, unit tests, or the implementer's narrative. Check whether context is genuinely readable and safe, and whether learning content helps remember the word itself rather than repeating a Chinese gloss or inventing a story. Return exactly: DECISION: accept|reject|insufficient-evidence; then concise evidence, metric validity, factual/provenance problems, regressions, and the single next question.

artifacts\agent-review-log.md:33830:docs\agentic-loop-status.md:14:- Regressions/limits: no build or existing test regressions; the 20-card blind-review files still contain no completed human decisions, so learning-layer judge pass rate and source factuality are not yet independently established. artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39185:-- Hypothesis: provenance must describe the actual displayed item, not merely its service. A WordNet definition or a prefix collision (for example `go` in `good`) cannot truthfully be presented as a target-word example; allowing only target-bearing example sentences will remove another class of false learning evidence.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39186:-- Change: `WordNetExampleUsageHintService` no longer falls back to definitions, and its matcher accepts only the exact target or a small conventional inflection set. New tests reject definition-only and `go`/`good` prefix cases while retaining `dwindle`/`dwindled`. This follows commit `78f5d85`, which suppresses legacy four-column morphology/family rows and adds provenance fields to future generated rows.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39187:-- Metric delta: on the same 200-word audit, the first fail-closed pass showed 200/200 purported WordNet examples. After requiring an actual target-bearing example, 113/200 cards retain source-labelled WordNet usage and 87/200 honestly omit a learning hook: `artifacts/card-audit-targeted-wordnet-20260901.tsv`. No remaining audit card shows a usage line without the matching evidence label. Executable suite: 21/21 passed. `dotnet build RealtimeTranslateCodex.sln --no-restore`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39189:-- Regressions/limits: 87/200 audit words now have no learning hook, so useful source-bearing coverage is 56.5%, below the 70% goal. Legacy TSV rows still lack field-level evidence; the generator currently writes one source/confidence per row, which is insufficient when breakdown and family came from different inputs. The independent read-only review of `78f5d85` was `insufficient-evidence`: there is no screenshot gold corpus, two-agent transcriptions, 30-word learning evaluation, regenerated production TSV, or completed blind reviewer report. OCR and learning completion thresholds remain unmeasured.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39190:-- Independent review: a fresh review is required after this committed change. Do not create `docs/agent-loop.auto-accepted.md` or modify `docs/agent-loop.accepted`.
artifacts\agent-review-log.md:39191:-- Next question: can the regenerated TSV carry separate evidence per displayed breakdown/family item and raise useful, source-bearing learning hooks to at least 70% in a blinded 30-word evaluation without reintroducing false provenance?

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Dictionary;

public sealed partial class WordNetExampleUsageHintService : IUsageHintService
{
    public UsageHintResult GetHint(DictionaryLookupResult lookup, SenseRankingResult ranking, string targetWord)
    {
        // An abstaining ranker may still expose a study-only comparison, but
        // every example must remain attached to its own sense. This keeps the
        // main definition undecided while giving the learner a useful way to
        // distinguish the candidates.
        var isMultiSenseComparison = ranking.SelectedSense is null;
        var senses = isMultiSenseComparison
            ? lookup.Senses ?? []
            : new[] { ranking.SelectedSense! };

        // A partial comparison is not neutral: displaying evidence for only
        // one candidate can quietly recreate the sense choice that the main
        // card deliberately abstained from. Restrict this study-only form to
        // a complete, compact two-way contrast.
        if (isMultiSenseComparison && senses.Count != 2)
        {
            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }

        var hints = senses
            .Select(sense =>
            {
                var examples = (sense.EnglishExamples ?? [])
                    .Where(candidate => ContainsTarget(candidate, targetWord))
                    .Select(candidate => ToShortHint(candidate, targetWord))
                    .Where(hint => hint.Length > 0)
                    .Distinct(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
                    .Take(2)
                    .ToArray();
                if (examples.Length == 0)
                {
                    return (Text: string.Empty, Examples: Array.Empty<string>());
                }

                var text = isMultiSenseComparison
                    ? $"{sense.PartOfSpeech}. {sense.ShortDefinition}：{string.Join(" · ", examples)}"
                    : string.Join(" · ", examples);
                return (Text: text, Examples: examples);
            })
            .Where(hint => hint.Text.Length > 0)
            .GroupBy(hint => hint.Text, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            .Select(group => group.First())
            .Take(2)
            .ToArray();
        if (isMultiSenseComparison && hints.Length != senses.Count)
        {
            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }
        if (hints.Length == 0)
        {
            // A definition can be accurate yet merely restate the Chinese
            // gloss. Only a target-bearing example is evidence of a distinct
            // study hook, so leave this layer empty when none is available.
            return UsageHintResult.Empty;
        }

        var examples = hints.SelectMany(hint => hint.Examples).ToArray();
        var exactCoverage = examples.Count(example => HasExactTarget(example, targetWord)) / (double)examples.Length;
        var confidence = 0.75 + exactCoverage * 0.15;
        var verification = exactCoverage == 1
            ? "例句直含目标�?
            : "例句含常规词�?;
        return new UsageHintResult(
            string.Join(" · ", hints.Select(hint => hint.Text)),
            $"Open English WordNet 2025；{verification}",
            confidence);
    }

    private static string ToShortHint(string example, string targetWord)
    {
        var words = WordToken().Matches(example).Select(match => match.Value).ToArray();
        if (words.Length == 0)
        {
            return string.Empty;
        }

        var targetIndex = Array.FindIndex(words, word => IsTargetForm(word, targetWord));
        var start = targetIndex < 0 ? 0 : Math.Max(0, targetIndex - 3);
        var end = targetIndex < 0 ? Math.Min(words.Length, 7) : Math.Min(words.Length, targetIndex + 4);
        var prefix = start > 0 ? "�? : string.Empty;
        var suffix = end < words.Length ? "�? : string.Empty;
        return $"{prefix}{string.Join(" ", words[start..end]).ToLowerInvariant()}{suffix}";
    }

    private static bool ContainsTarget(string text, string targetWord) =>
        WordToken().Matches(text).Any(match => IsTargetForm(match.Value, targetWord));

    private static bool HasExactTarget(string text, string targetWord) =>
        WordToken().Matches(text).Any(match => match.Value.Equals(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

    private static bool IsTargetForm(string word, string targetWord)
    {
        if (word.Equals(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
        {
            return true;
        }

        // Do not let a prefix match turn "go" into evidence for "good".
        // This is intentionally a small inflection whitelist rather than a
        // general stemmer: a displayed example must visibly contain the word
        // or a conventional surface inflection of it.
        if (word.StartsWith(targetWord, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && IsInflectionSuffix(word[targetWord.Length..]))
        {
            return true;
        }

        return targetWord.EndsWith('e')
            && word.StartsWith(targetWord[..^1], StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
            && IsInflectionSuffix(word[(targetWord.Length - 1)..]);
    }

    private static bool IsInflectionSuffix(string suffix) => suffix.Equals("s", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("es", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("d", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("ed", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("ing", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("er", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        || suffix.Equals("est", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    [GeneratedRegex("[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)?")]
    private static partial Regex WordToken();
}

# Iteration 1

## Hypothesis

The fixed 180 px vertical context padding may crop out nearby Reverse: 1999 dialogue text. A modest increase to 240 px in both live and replay capture was expected to recover more sentence text without changing the general desktop selection mode.

## Exact Change And Commit

The experiment changed `ContextVerticalPaddingPixels` from 180 to 240 in `WindowsScreenshotService` and `ReplayScreenshotService`, then reverted it after verification. The final committed state keeps the original 180 px behavior because the measured result was a regression. Commits: `1940132` (report/status) and `0e26673` (independent-review correction).

## Before/After Examples

The deterministic archive subset was indices 200 (`parrot`), 500 (`frail`), 939 (`thrust`), 1123 (`bark`), and 1127 (`bark`). Before, the existing 180 px replay evidence (`artifacts/context-unmasked-full-after-20260901.json`) had no replay timeouts on the 20-sample corpus; indices 1123 and 1127 safely abstained/selected respectively. After the temporary 240 px change, the three dialogue samples still returned the same visible context and meanings, while both HUD-heavy bark samples timed out. No sentence-edge recovery was observed.

## Metrics

The prior 20-sample production replay was 20/20 exact OCR, 16 labelled context cases, 14/16 context Top-1, and 4/4 correct abstentions with 0 timeouts/failures. The 240 px focused replay was 5/5 exact OCR, 3/3 context-labelled and 3/3 context Top-1 among completed context cases, 2/2 correct abstentions, but had 2 replay timeouts and 2 replay failures (`artifacts/iteration-1-padding240.json`). The executable test suite remained 23/23, and the Debug build had 0 warnings and 0 errors; these do not establish OCR usefulness.

## Regressions And Limits

The larger crop increased OCR work enough to time out both `bark` HUD samples. It did not improve the observed `parrot`, `frail`, or `thrust` transcription. The experiment used five archived screenshots, not the required 50-screenshot two-agent gold corpus, and provides no new learning-usefulness evidence. The temporary code was reverted, so the shipped behavior has no net OCR regression.

## Independent Review

Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed that 240 px caused two HUD replay timeouts and that the three completed dialogue samples showed no changed text. The reviewer also noted that the five-case result has no independently transcribed line-level gold labels or WER, and that the 5/5 OCR figure must not be read as end-to-end success because two samples failed. The reviewer found no basis for automatic acceptance.

## Next Question

Can a detected, optional dialogue-region enhancement choose a smaller text-bearing crop (using screenshot content signals) so that context OCR improves without expanding every general desktop crop or increasing HUD timeouts?

+
+## Exact Change And Commit
+
+The experiment changed `ContextVerticalPaddingPixels` from 180 to 240 in `WindowsScreenshotService` and `ReplayScreenshotService`, then reverted it after verification. The final committed state keeps the original 180 px behavior because the measured result was a regression. This report and the status update are committed as the iteration record.
+
+## Before/After Examples
+
+The deterministic archive subset was indices 200 (`parrot`), 500 (`frail`), 939 (`thrust`), 1123 (`bark`), and 1127 (`bark`). Before, the existing 180 px replay evidence (`artifacts/context-unmasked-full-after-20260901.json`) had no replay timeouts on the 20-sample corpus; indices 1123 and 1127 safely abstained/selected respectively. After the temporary 240 px change, the three dialogue samples still returned the same visible context and meanings, while both HUD-heavy bark samples timed out. No sentence-edge recovery was observed.
+
+## Metrics
+
+The prior 20-sample production replay was 20/20 exact OCR, 16 labelled context cases, 14/16 context Top-1, and 4/4 correct abstentions with 0 timeouts/failures. The 240 px focused replay was 5/5 exact OCR, 3/3 context-labelled and 3/3 context Top-1 among completed context cases, 2/2 correct abstentions, but had 2 replay timeouts and 2 replay failures (`artifacts/iteration-1-padding240.json`). The executable test suite remained 23/23, and the Debug build had 0 warnings and 0 errors; these do not establish OCR usefulness.
+
+## Regressions And Limits
+
+The larger crop increased OCR work enough to time out both `bark` HUD samples. It did not improve the observed `parrot`, `frail`, or `thrust` transcription. The experiment used five archived screenshots, not the required 50-screenshot two-agent gold corpus, and provides no new learning-usefulness evidence. The temporary code was reverted, so the shipped behavior has no net OCR regression.
+
+## Independent Review
+
+`insufficient-evidence`: the experiment is a falsified crop-size hypothesis, not an accepted improvement. A reviewer must confirm that the timeout regression and unchanged dialogue text are correctly represented; no automatic acceptance is warranted.
+
+## Next Question
+
+Can a detected, optional dialogue-region enhancement choose a smaller text-bearing crop (using screenshot content signals) so that context OCR improves without expanding every general desktop crop or increasing HUD timeouts?

+# Iteration 1
+
+## Hypothesis
+
+The fixed 180 px vertical context padding may crop out nearby Reverse: 1999 dialogue text. A modest increase to 240 px in both live and replay capture was expected to recover more sentence text without changing the general desktop selection mode.
+
+## Exact Change And Commit
+
+The experiment changed `ContextVerticalPaddingPixels` from 180 to 240 in `WindowsScreenshotService` and `ReplayScreenshotService`, then reverted it after verification. The final committed state keeps the original 180 px behavior because the measured result was a regression. Commits: `1940132` (report/status) and `0e26673` (independent-review correction).
+
+## Before/After Examples
+
+The deterministic archive subset was indices 200 (`parrot`), 500 (`frail`), 939 (`thrust`), 1123 (`bark`), and 1127 (`bark`). Before, the existing 180 px replay evidence (`artifacts/context-unmasked-full-after-20260901.json`) had no replay timeouts on the 20-sample corpus; indices 1123 and 1127 safely abstained/selected respectively. After the temporary 240 px change, the three dialogue samples still returned the same visible context and meanings, while both HUD-heavy bark samples timed out. No sentence-edge recovery was observed.
+
+## Metrics
+
+The prior 20-sample production replay was 20/20 exact OCR, 16 labelled context cases, 14/16 context Top-1, and 4/4 correct abstentions with 0 timeouts/failures. The 240 px focused replay was 5/5 exact OCR, 3/3 context-labelled and 3/3 context Top-1 among completed context cases, 2/2 correct abstentions, but had 2 replay timeouts and 2 replay failures (`artifacts/iteration-1-padding240.json`). The executable test suite remained 23/23, and the Debug build had 0 warnings and 0 errors; these do not establish OCR usefulness.
+
+## Regressions And Limits
+
+The larger crop increased OCR work enough to time out both `bark` HUD samples. It did not improve the observed `parrot`, `frail`, or `thrust` transcription. The experiment used five archived screenshots, not the required 50-screenshot two-agent gold corpus, and provides no new learning-usefulness evidence. The temporary code was reverted, so the shipped behavior has no net OCR regression.
+
+## Independent Review
+
+Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed that 240 px caused two HUD replay timeouts and that the three completed dialogue samples showed no changed text. The reviewer also noted that the five-case result has no independently transcribed line-level gold labels or WER, and that the 5/5 OCR figure must not be read as end-to-end success because two samples failed. The reviewer found no basis for automatic acceptance.
+
+## Next Question
+
+Can a detected, optional dialogue-region enhancement choose a smaller text-bearing crop (using screenshot content signals) so that context OCR improves without expanding every general desktop crop or increasing HUD timeouts?

+# Iteration 1
+
+## Hypothesis
+
+The fixed 180 px vertical context padding may crop out nearby Reverse: 1999 dialogue text. A modest increase to 240 px in both live and replay capture was expected to recover more sentence text without changing the general desktop selection mode.
+
+## Exact Change And Commit
+
+The experiment changed `ContextVerticalPaddingPixels` from 180 to 240 in `WindowsScreenshotService` and `ReplayScreenshotService`, then reverted it after verification. The final committed state keeps the original 180 px behavior because the measured result was a regression. Commits: `1940132` (report/status) and `0e26673` (independent-review correction).
+
+## Before/After Examples
+
+The deterministic archive subset was indices 200 (`parrot`), 500 (`frail`), 939 (`thrust`), 1123 (`bark`), and 1127 (`bark`). Before, the existing 180 px replay evidence (`artifacts/context-unmasked-full-after-20260901.json`) had no replay timeouts on the 20-sample corpus; indices 1123 and 1127 safely abstained/selected respectively. After the temporary 240 px change, the three dialogue samples still returned the same visible context and meanings, while both HUD-heavy bark samples timed out. No sentence-edge recovery was observed.
+
+## Metrics
+
+The prior 20-sample production replay was 20/20 exact OCR, 16 labelled context cases, 14/16 context Top-1, and 4/4 correct abstentions with 0 timeouts/failures. The 240 px focused replay was 5/5 exact OCR, 3/3 context-labelled and 3/3 context Top-1 among completed context cases, 2/2 correct abstentions, but had 2 replay timeouts and 2 replay failures (`artifacts/iteration-1-padding240.json`). The executable test suite remained 23/23, and the Debug build had 0 warnings and 0 errors; these do not establish OCR usefulness.
+
+## Regressions And Limits
+
+The larger crop increased OCR work enough to time out both `bark` HUD samples. It did not improve the observed `parrot`, `frail`, or `thrust` transcription. The experiment used five archived screenshots, not the required 50-screenshot two-agent gold corpus, and provides no new learning-usefulness evidence. The temporary code was reverted, so the shipped behavior has no net OCR regression.
+
+## Independent Review
+
+Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed that 240 px caused two HUD replay timeouts and that the three completed dialogue samples showed no changed text. The reviewer also noted that the five-case result has no independently transcribed line-level gold labels or WER, and that the 5/5 OCR figure must not be read as end-to-end success because two samples failed. The reviewer found no basis for automatic acceptance.
+
+## Next Question
+
+Can a detected, optional dialogue-region enhancement choose a smaller text-bearing crop (using screenshot content signals) so that context OCR improves without expanding every general desktop crop or increasing HUD timeouts?

+# Iteration 2
+
+## Hypothesis
+
+The OCR selector was too conservative for context crops: requiring two additional usable tokens meant a scaled or binarized variant that recovered only one sentence token was discarded. Allowing a one-token upgrade only when the first result already has multiple usable tokens should recover dialogue edges while preserving tight word OCR stability.
+
+## Exact Changes And Commit
+
+`src/RealtimeTranslate.Core/Ocr/OcrVariantSelector.cs` now uses a required gain of 2 for one-token crops and 1 for multi-token crops. `tests/RealtimeTranslate.Tests/Program.cs` adds a marginal-context regression case proving the recovered-token path. The final coherent commit is recorded below after verification.
+
+## Before/After Examples
+
+On the comparable 20-sample archived game set, several context strings gained one recovered token. Index 1029 changed from a truncated context ending before the target to one including `the`; index 1028 gained the trailing `my`; other changed samples included 657, 700, 845, 939, 1030, and 1090. Some outputs remain visibly mangled, so these are examples of recovery, not proof of transcription quality. Tight word behavior remained unchanged in the `bark` selector test.
+
+## Metrics
+
+Before: exact word OCR 20/20, context available 16/16, context Top-1 10/16, replay timeouts/failures 0/0. After: exact word OCR 20/20, context available 16/16, context Top-1 11/16, replay timeouts/failures 0/0, and OCR regressions 0 (`artifacts/variant-selection-before-20260901.json`, `artifacts/variant-selection-after-20260901.json`, `artifacts/iteration-2-selector-after-20260901.json`). Focused executable tests passed 23/23 (including the new marginal-context assertions); build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
+
+## Regressions And Limits
+
+The selector still chooses by usable-token count, so a multi-token general desktop crop could admit a noisier variant with one extra token. The synthetic test does not cover that adversarial case. The replay set has no independent line-level gold transcription or WER, is below the required 50 screenshots, and does not measure learning usefulness. The change is reversible in one selector rule and did not regress observed word OCR or replay stability.
+
+## Independent Review
+
+Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed the 20/20 exact OCR, 0 timeouts/failures, and context Top-1 improvement from 10/16 to 11/16, but found no basis for acceptance without line-level fidelity labels, WER, context-gate precision/recall, and a general desktop noise corpus.
+
+## Next Question
+
+Can a 50-plus screenshot, two-reviewer line-level gold corpus show that the one-token context upgrade improves WER and dialogue-line recovery without admitting noisy variants in arbitrary desktop selections?

         // A tight word crop normally has one meaningful token in every
         // variant. Do not replace that known-good first result on a marginal
-        // score difference. Context OCR needs a clear extra sentence token
-        // before another preprocessing result can take over.
-        return best.Score >= firstScore + 2 ? best.Candidates : first;
+        // score difference. For multi-token crops, a one-token gain is useful
+        // evidence that a scaled/preprocessed variant recovered a sentence
+        // edge, so allow that upgrade without changing single-word behavior.
+        var requiredGain = firstScore <= 1 ? 2 : 1;
+        return best.Score >= firstScore + requiredGain ? best.Candidates : first;
     }

# Iteration 2

## Hypothesis

The OCR selector was too conservative for context crops: requiring two additional usable tokens meant a scaled or binarized variant that recovered only one sentence token was discarded. Allowing a one-token upgrade only when the first result already has multiple usable tokens should recover dialogue edges while preserving tight word OCR stability.

## Exact Changes And Commit

`src/RealtimeTranslate.Core/Ocr/OcrVariantSelector.cs` now uses a required gain of 2 for one-token crops and 1 for multi-token crops. `tests/RealtimeTranslate.Tests/Program.cs` adds a marginal-context regression case proving the recovered-token path. The final coherent commit is recorded below after verification.

## Before/After Examples

On the comparable 20-sample archived game set, several context strings gained one recovered token. Index 1029 changed from a truncated context ending before the target to one including `the`; index 1028 gained the trailing `my`; other changed samples included 657, 700, 845, 939, 1030, and 1090. Some outputs remain visibly mangled, so these are examples of recovery, not proof of transcription quality. Tight word behavior remained unchanged in the `bark` selector test.

## Metrics

Before: exact word OCR 20/20, context available 16/16, context Top-1 10/16, replay timeouts/failures 0/0. After: exact word OCR 20/20, context available 16/16, context Top-1 11/16, replay timeouts/failures 0/0, and OCR regressions 0 (`artifacts/variant-selection-before-20260901.json`, `artifacts/variant-selection-after-20260901.json`, `artifacts/iteration-2-selector-after-20260901.json`). Focused executable tests passed 23/23 (including the new marginal-context assertions); build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

## Regressions And Limits

The selector still chooses by usable-token count, so a multi-token general desktop crop could admit a noisier variant with one extra token. The synthetic test does not cover that adversarial case. The replay set has no independent line-level gold transcription or WER, is below the required 50 screenshots, and does not measure learning usefulness. The change is reversible in one selector rule and did not regress observed word OCR or replay stability.

## Independent Review

Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed the 20/20 exact OCR, 0 timeouts/failures, and context Top-1 improvement from 10/16 to 11/16, but found no basis for acceptance without line-level fidelity labels, WER, context-gate precision/recall, and a general desktop noise corpus.

## Next Question

Can a 50-plus screenshot, two-reviewer line-level gold corpus show that the one-token context upgrade improves WER and dialogue-line recovery without admitting noisy variants in arbitrary desktop selections?

# Agentic Loop Status

Updated: 2026-09-01 14:05:00

- Run: agent iteration 1
- Stage: improving usable context OCR and learning-card quality
- Goal: reliable sentence understanding plus memorable word learning
- Scope: general desktop OCR baseline plus optional game-dialogue enhancement
- Independent review: required after each relevant committed change
- Completion: automatic threshold or user acceptance
- Hypothesis: increasing context vertical padding from 180 px to 240 px would recover cropped dialogue lines.
- Result: rejected; focused replay showed no dialogue gain and 2 HUD OCR timeouts, so the temporary code was reverted.
- Independent review: insufficient-evidence; no automatic acceptance.
- Next: test detected, optional dialogue-region cropping with bounded OCR cost.
# Iteration 1

## Hypothesis

The fixed 180 px vertical context padding may crop out nearby Reverse: 1999 dialogue text. A modest increase to 240 px in both live and replay capture was expected to recover more sentence text without changing the general desktop selection mode.

## Exact Change And Commit

The experiment changed `ContextVerticalPaddingPixels` from 180 to 240 in `WindowsScreenshotService` and `ReplayScreenshotService`, then reverted it after verification. The final committed state keeps the original 180 px behavior because the measured result was a regression. Commits: `1940132` (report/status) and `0e26673` (independent-review correction).

## Before/After Examples

The deterministic archive subset was indices 200 (`parrot`), 500 (`frail`), 939 (`thrust`), 1123 (`bark`), and 1127 (`bark`). Before, the existing 180 px replay evidence (`artifacts/context-unmasked-full-after-20260901.json`) had no replay timeouts on the 20-sample corpus; indices 1123 and 1127 safely abstained/selected respectively. After the temporary 240 px change, the three dialogue samples still returned the same visible context and meanings, while both HUD-heavy bark samples timed out. No sentence-edge recovery was observed.

## Metrics

The prior 20-sample production replay was 20/20 exact OCR, 16 labelled context cases, 14/16 context Top-1, and 4/4 correct abstentions with 0 timeouts/failures. The 240 px focused replay was 5/5 exact OCR, 3/3 context-labelled and 3/3 context Top-1 among completed context cases, 2/2 correct abstentions, but had 2 replay timeouts and 2 replay failures (`artifacts/iteration-1-padding240.json`). The executable test suite remained 23/23, and the Debug build had 0 warnings and 0 errors; these do not establish OCR usefulness.

## Regressions And Limits

The larger crop increased OCR work enough to time out both `bark` HUD samples. It did not improve the observed `parrot`, `frail`, or `thrust` transcription. The experiment used five archived screenshots, not the required 50-screenshot two-agent gold corpus, and provides no new learning-usefulness evidence. The temporary code was reverted, so the shipped behavior has no net OCR regression.

## Independent Review

Decision: `insufficient-evidence`. The independent reviewer confirmed that 240 px caused two HUD replay timeouts and that the three completed dialogue samples showed no changed text. The reviewer also noted that the five-case result has no independently transcribed line-level gold labels or WER, and that the 5/5 OCR figure must not be read as end-to-end success because two samples failed. The reviewer found no basis for automatic acceptance.

## Next Question

Can a detected, optional dialogue-region enhancement choose a smaller text-bearing crop (using screenshot content signals) so that context OCR improves without expanding every general desktop crop or increasing HUD timeouts?

using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Ocr;

/// <summary>Chooses a stable OCR variant without treating first non-empty output as success.</summary>
public static partial class OcrVariantSelector
{
    public static IReadOnlyList<OcrCandidate> Select(IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyList<OcrCandidate>> variants)
    {
        var nonEmpty = variants
            .Where(variant => variant.Any(candidate => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(candidate.Text)))
            .ToArray();
        if (nonEmpty.Length == 0)
        {
            return [];
        }

        var first = nonEmpty[0];
        var firstScore = UsableTokenCount(first);
        var best = nonEmpty
            .Select((variant, index) => new RankedVariant(variant, UsableTokenCount(variant), index))
            .OrderByDescending(item => item.Score)
            .ThenBy(item => item.Index)
            .First();

        // A tight word crop normally has one meaningful token in every
        // variant. Do not replace that known-good first result on a marginal
        // score difference. For multi-token crops, a one-token gain is useful
        // evidence that a scaled/preprocessed variant recovered a sentence
        // edge, so allow that upgrade without changing single-word behavior.
        var requiredGain = firstScore <= 1 ? 2 : 1;
        return best.Score >= firstScore + requiredGain ? best.Candidates : first;
    }

    private static int UsableTokenCount(IReadOnlyList<OcrCandidate> candidates) => candidates.Count(candidate =>
        WordToken().IsMatch(candidate.Text.Trim()) && candidate.Text.Trim().Length >= 2);

    private sealed record RankedVariant(IReadOnlyList<OcrCandidate> Candidates, int Score, int Index);

    [GeneratedRegex("^[A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)?$")]
    private static partial Regex WordToken();
}
    using var writer = new StreamWriter(outputPath, false, new System.Text.UTF8Encoding(false));
    writer.WriteLine("archive index\tscreenshot\ttarget\tmanual transcription\tobserved OCR context\texpected trust\tactual trust\tprimary meaning\tbefore first-screen lines\tafter first-screen lines");
    foreach (var sample in cases)
    {
        var normalized = normalizer.Normalize(sample.Word);
        var lookup = dictionary.Lookup(normalized);
        var ranking = ranker.Rank(lookup, normalized, sample.Ocr);
        AssertEqual(sample.Expected, ranking.ContextStatus);
        var presentation = new LookupPresentation(
            normalized.DisplayWord,
            $"lemma: {lookup.EntryWord}",
            ranking.Definitions,
            ranking.PrimaryDefinition,
            1,
            FrequencyBand: lookup.FrequencyBand,
            ContextStatus: ranking.ContextStatus);
        var after = string.Join(" | ", LookupCardTextFormatter.VisibleLines(presentation).Take(3));
        var beforeStatus = ranking.WasContextAligned
            ? "整句句意对齐：已用于筛�?
            : "整句句意对齐：未用于筛�?;
        var before = string.Join(" | ", new[] { $"{presentation.Title} {LookupCardTextFormatter.Frequency(presentation.FrequencyBand)}".Trim(), presentation.PrimaryDefinition, beforeStatus });
        writer.WriteLine(string.Join('\t', new[]
        {
            sample.Index.ToString(), sample.Screenshot, sample.Word, sample.Manual, sample.Ocr,
            sample.Expected.ToString(), ranking.ContextStatus.ToString(), ranking.PrimaryDefinition, before, after,
        }.Select(value => value.Replace('\t', ' ').Replace('\r', ' ').Replace('\n', ' '))));
    }
}

static string CreateInsightFixture()
{
    var root = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "realtime-translate-tests", Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N"));
    Directory.CreateDirectory(root);
    File.WriteAllText(
        Path.Combine(root, "word-cards.tsv"),
        "ineffable\tineffable（词基：无法形容的）\teffable,ineffability\tsacred mysteries\tMorphoLex (2018)\t0.75");
    return root;
}

static void AssertEqual<T>(T expected, T actual)
{
    if (!EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals(expected, actual))
    {
        throw new InvalidOperationException($"expected '{expected}', got '{actual}'");
    }
}

static void AssertTrue(bool value, string message)
{
    if (!value)
    {
        throw new InvalidOperationException(message);
    }
}

static string FindBundledDictionary()
{
    return Path.Combine(FindAppSourceDirectory(), "dictionary.tsv");
}

static string FindRepositoryRoot()
{
    return Directory.GetParent(Directory.GetParent(FindAppSourceDirectory())!.FullName)!.FullName;
}

static string FindAppSourceDirectory()
{
    var directory = new DirectoryInfo(AppContext.BaseDirectory);
    while (directory is not null)
    {
        var path = Path.Combine(directory.FullName, "src", "RealtimeTranslate.App");
        if (File.Exists(Path.Combine(path, "dictionary.tsv")))
        {
            return path;
        }

        directory = directory.Parent;
    }

    throw new DirectoryNotFoundException("Could not locate src/RealtimeTranslate.App.");
}

internal sealed class StaticResponseHandler : HttpMessageHandler
{
    private readonly string _responseBody;

    public StaticResponseHandler(string responseBody)
    {
        _responseBody = responseBody;
    }

    protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var response = new HttpResponseMessage(System.Net.HttpStatusCode.OK)
        {
            Content = new StringContent(_responseBody),
        };
        return Task.FromResult(response);
    }
}

# Agentic Loop: 可靠上下�?OCR + 能帮助记忆的单词�?

## 目标

工具必须同时解决两件事：

1. 用户马上理解当前游戏句子中该词的意思；
2. 用户随后能理解并记住这个词本身，而非只记住这一次的中文答案�?

错误或乱码的上下文绝不能驱动释义。反过来，正确的本句义也不应挤掉对单词核心概念、搭配和记忆线索的解释�?

## 上下�?OCR 的量化门�?

建立至少 50 条真实游戏截图的金标准语料。每条记录截图、选词、人工转录的目标字幕行、关键内容词、可接受断句；两个独�?agent 的盲转写一致才计入金标准，分歧样本标为 `uncertain`，不得伪造真值�?

- 目标所在字幕行恢复�?�?5%�?
- 上下�?normalized WER �?%，或关键内容词准确率 �?2%�?
- `ContextQualityGate` 对“可安全用于推义”的 precision �?5%、recall �?5%�?
- 依赖上下文的词义 Top-1 �?0%；低质量上下文强行影响主释义�?0�?
- P95 从松开选择到基础�?�? 秒�?

必须探索并按实证选择：行�?OCR 输出（含几何位置）、多尺度与多预处理结果、候选行融合、以选区为锚点的字幕区裁剪、以及可信度门控。不得把首个非空 OCR 结果当作成功；不得通过词典猜测伪�?OCR 原文；低可信上下文必须明确降级�?

## 学习型卡片的完成定义

卡片分为两层�?

- **首屏（继续读剧情�?*：原�?词形、当前句义、词性、短语或句子功能、上下文可信状态。最多五块；网络不可用也必须出现�?
- **学习层（记住这个词）**：只保留经证据支持、最有助记忆�?1�? 项：词的核心概念、常见搭�?短语、可信的词形关系或构词线索、以及一个能区分易混义项的例子。它不能是空泛的 AI 套话、冗长词典复制或不可靠词源故事�?

实现时允许替换词典数据结构、增加带来源�?`LearningInsight`、使用不�?OCR/词典/模型服务。但每条学习信息必须标记来源和置信度；AI 增强只能异步出现，失败时不影响首屏�?

## 学习质量量化门槛

对至�?30 个真实游戏词建立学习评测集（含普通词、抽象词、词形变化、搭配、专有称谓和多义词）。每项有可验证的核心释义、至少一个不可接受的空泛/错误解释及来源�?

- 独立评委对“首屏可继续阅读”判定通过 �?0%�?
- 独立评委对“学习层能帮助理解词本身而非重复中文释义”判定通过 �?0%�?
- 学习层事�?来源错误�?0；空泛、无证据或重复信息比�?�?0%�?
- 至少 70% 样本提供一条有用且可信的记忆线索；其余必须诚实省略，不能硬凑�?

## 独立评委与停止条�?

对每个改�?OCR、上下文选择、可信度或学习卡架构的提交，runner 启动一个全新、只�?reviewer agent。评委必须审查截图、金标准、前后输出和实际卡片，只能输�?`accept`、`reject` �?`insufficient-evidence`，不能修改文件，也不能仅凭实现者的文字或单元测试认可方案�?

达到全部 OCR 与学习门槛，并在两批未参与开发的样本上连续获得两个独立评�?`accept` 后，agent 创建 `docs/agent-loop.auto-accepted.md` 写明证据与两份评审报告，runner 自动停止。这是自动研究完成，不等同于用户最终验收�?

每轮只解决最高价值差距；不删除用户文件、归档截图或历史记录；不回到托盘、热键等无关工作�?

MorphoLex-derived confidence is a conservative default for legacy rows, not a per-entry audit.

docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:1:# Agentic Loop: 可靠上下�?OCR + 能帮助记忆的单词�?docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:12:## 上下�?OCR 的量化门�?docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:22:必须探索并按实证选择：行�?OCR 输出（含几何位置）、多尺度与多预处理结果、候选行融合、以选区为锚点的字幕区裁剪、以及可信度门控。不得把首个非空 OCR 结果当作成功；不得通过词典猜测伪�?OCR 原文；低可信上下文必须明确降级�?docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:31:实现时允许替换词典数据结构、增加带来源�?`LearningInsight`、使用不�?OCR/词典/模型服务。但每条学习信息必须标记来源和置信度；AI 增强只能异步出现，失败时不影响首屏�?docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:44:对每个改�?OCR、上下文选择、可信度或学习卡架构的提交，runner 启动一个全新、只�?reviewer agent。评委必须审查截图、金标准、前后输出和实际卡片，只能输�?`accept`、`reject` �?`insufficient-evidence`，不能修改文件，也不能仅凭实现者的文字或单元测试认可方案�?docs\agentic-loop-goal.md:46:达到全部 OCR 与学习门槛，并在两批未参与开发的样本上连续获得两个独立评�?`accept` 后，agent 创建 `docs/agent-loop.auto-accepted.md` 写明证据与两份评审报告，runner 自动停止。这是自动研究完成，不等同于用户最终验收�?src\RealtimeTranslate.App\Settings\UserPreferencesStore.cs:38:            var manualHotkey = ParseHotkey(dto.ManualLookupHotkeyKey, dto.ManualLookupHotkeyModifiers, UserPreferences.Default.ManualLookupHotkey);

docs\plans\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-workflow.md:2:intent: Add Tab completion to manual lookup by reusing the recent lookup history as the completion source.
docs\plans\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-workflow.md:3:success_criteria: Typing a previously looked-up word prefix in manual lookup and pressing Tab completes to the most recent matching history word, and Enter submits it.

docs\agentic-loop-status.md:6:- Stage: improving usable context OCR and learning-card quality
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:8:- Independent review: required after each relevant committed change
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:10:- Hypothesis: learning metadata was presented as unexplained prose; attaching evidence source and confidence will reduce unsupported learning claims without displacing the sentence gloss.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:11:- Change: `WordInsight` now carries `EvidenceSource`/`Confidence`; legacy four-column MorphoLex rows receive the licensed MorphoLex (2018) source and 0.75 confidence when non-empty. WordNet fallback usage is labelled separately at 90% confidence. Cards render a distinct `证据` line, after sentence meaning and alignment.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:12:- Metric delta: baseline evidence-labelled learning blocks 0/20 in `blind-card-review-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json`; after this change, every non-empty insight is source-bearing by construction, and fallback usage is source-bearing. Automated suite: 19/19 checks passed (including new evidence presentation check). OCR replay metrics unchanged (20/20 exact; 15/16 context Top-1 on labelled samples).
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:13:- Real examples: `bark` with “The dog began to bark�?remains a verb gloss and now gets explicit evidence metadata; the HUD-only `bark` sample remains abstention-safe and does not gain a guessed sense. `exquisite` keeps “精致的�?on the first screen while its study metadata is separately attributed.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:14:- Regressions/limits: no build or existing test regressions; the 20-card blind-review files still contain no completed human decisions, so learning-layer judge pass rate and source factuality are not yet independently established. MorphoLex-derived confidence is a conservative default for legacy rows, not a per-entry audit.
docs\agentic-loop-status.md:15:- Next question: run a fresh blind card review on the evidence-labelled output and audit whether the 0.75 default should be lowered or replaced with per-entry reviewed confidence.

docs\agent-loop-status.md:5:- Run: isolated replay evidence by accepting `--replay-output` in the app and assigning each verifier invocation and child replay a unique temporary lookup-record file. `Verify-ReplayCorpus.ps1` also recognizes the current explicit-abstention prefix. This prevents concurrent replay processes from shifting one card's output onto another source index.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:6:- Evidence: the clean real Debug replay of all 20 game screenshots completed with zero timeouts/failures, `ocr_exact=20/20`, `dictionary_found=20/20`, `top1_sense=15/16`, available context `16/16`, context top-1 `15/16`, and labelled abstentions `4/4`: `artifacts/blind-review-source-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json`. `dotnet build RealtimeTranslateCodex.sln --no-restore` completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; the executable suite passed 19/19.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:7:- Blind-review evidence: `artifacts/blind-card-review-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json` was generated from that clean source. It contains 20 actual cards with all 20 decisions and rationales blank; card fields contain no expected sense/outcome or automated verdict. It is genuinely unreviewed and includes the new uncertainty wording.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:8:- Remaining blocker: an independent human must complete that packet’s blinded `understandable` / `unclear` / `should-abstain` decision and rationale. No code change can supply this judgement; without it the product has neither the required human result nor the required 16 directly understood cards.
docs\agent-loop-status.md:9:- Next: have a reviewer complete `artifacts/blind-card-review-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json` without opening `tests/Data/replay-expected.json`, then run `pwsh -File tools/Test-BlindCardReview.ps1 -ReviewPath <completed-review.json> -SummaryPath artifacts/blind-review-source-explicit-uncertainty-clean-20260831.json -OutputPath artifacts/blind-review-reconciliation-<date>.json`. Treat every mismatch, `unclear` decision, or inappropriate certainty as the next single content repair. Do not create or modify `docs/agent-loop.accepted`.

docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:8:intent: Add Tab completion to manual lookup by reusing the recent lookup history as the completion source.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:11:- Preserve the existing manual lookup Enter and Escape behavior.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:13:- Keep completion matching reusable behind the recent lookup abstraction instead of making the manual input window parse history records directly.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:17:- When a word has already been looked up, typing a prefix in manual lookup and pressing Tab completes to the most recent matching history word.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:18:- Pressing Enter after completion submits the completed word for lookup.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:28:- confirm: the WPF app project builds and the manual lookup window accepts reusable completion candidates without changing existing submit/cancel behavior.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:33:- Human approval of this design before implementation.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:39:- Codex implements and verifies the change; the user reviews the final behavior.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:46:| Manual lookup UI | Apply Tab completion from history-backed candidates. | Add dropdowns, fuzzy search, or multi-candidate selection UI. |
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:63:The recent lookup store interface gains a reusable operation for asking history to complete a manual lookup prefix.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:69:The manual lookup window remains responsible for keyboard handling and submission. It receives a completion provider rather than reading recent lookup records itself.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:72:Expected implementation work is limited to the recent lookup interface and implementation, manual lookup window construction/keyboard handling, controller wiring, and focused tests.
docs\designs\2026-06-19-manual-lookup-tab-completion-design.md:76:- WPF Tab normally participates in focus traversal, so the window must intercept it before focus handling moves away from the input.

using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Presentation;

public static class LookupCardTextFormatter
{
    public static string Frequency(int band) => band switch
    {
        3 => "★★�?,
        2 => "★★�?,
        1 => "★☆�?,
        _ => string.Empty,
    };

    public static string Breakdown(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.WordBreakdown) ? string.Empty : $"词基/构词  {presentation.WordBreakdown}";

    public static string Family(LookupPresentation presentation) => presentation.WordFamily is { Count: > 0 }
        ? $"词族/词形  {string.Join(" · ", presentation.WordFamily.Take(3))}"
        : string.Empty;

    public static string Usage(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.ContextHint) ? string.Empty : $"用法/语境  {presentation.ContextHint}";

    public static string Evidence(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(presentation.InsightEvidence)
            ? string.Empty
            : $"证据  {presentation.InsightEvidence}";

    public static string ContextAlignment(LookupPresentation presentation) =>
        presentation.IsContextAligned ? "整句句意对齐：已用于筛�? : "整句句意对齐：未用于筛�?;

    public static IReadOnlyList<string> VisibleLines(LookupPresentation presentation)
    {
        var core = new[]
        {
            $"{presentation.Title} {Frequency(presentation.FrequencyBand)}".Trim(),
            presentation.PrimaryDefinition,
            presentation.IsError ? string.Empty : ContextAlignment(presentation),
        }.Where(line => line.Length > 0).ToList();

        // Keep the first screen compact: sentence meaning and usage outrank
        // study metadata. Show at most one optional metadata block so the
        // card never grows beyond five visible information blocks.
        var metadata = Breakdown(presentation);
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(metadata))
        {
            metadata = Family(presentation);
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(metadata))
        {
            core.Add(metadata);
        }

        var usage = Usage(presentation);
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(usage))
        {
            core.Add(usage);
        }

        var evidence = Evidence(presentation);
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(evidence))
        {
            core.Add(evidence);
        }

        return core.Take(5).ToArray();
    }
}
### insight parser
using RealtimeTranslate.Core.Models;

namespace RealtimeTranslate.Core.Dictionary;

public sealed class MorphemeWordInsightService : IWordInsightService
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, WordInsight> _entries = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

    public MorphemeWordInsightService(string wordCardsTsvPath)
    {
        if (!File.Exists(wordCardsTsvPath))
        {
            return;
        }
        foreach (var line in File.ReadLines(wordCardsTsvPath))
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line) || line.StartsWith('#'))
            {
                continue;
            }

            var fields = line.Split('\t');
            if (fields.Length < 4)
            {
                continue;
            }

            var word = fields[0].Trim();
            if (word.Length == 0)
            {
                continue;
            }

            var source = fields.Length >= 5 ? fields[4].Trim() : "MorphoLex (2018)";
            var confidence = fields.Length >= 6 && double.TryParse(fields[5], out var parsed)
                ? Math.Clamp(parsed, 0, 1)
                : (fields[1].Trim().Length > 0 || fields[3].Trim().Length > 0 ? 0.75 : 0);

            _entries[word] = new WordInsight(
                fields[1].Trim(),
                fields[2].Split(',', StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries | StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries),
                fields[3].Trim(),
                source,
                confidence);
        }
    }

    public WordInsight Lookup(string word)
    {
        return _entries.TryGetValue(word.Trim(), out var insight) ? insight : WordInsight.Empty;
    }
}
